column1: # Corana et al. (1987) protocol-replication reference table.
# Source (the ONLY permitted source for the numbers below):
#   A. Corana, M. Marchesi, C. Martini, S. Ridella,
#   "Minimizing multimodal functions of continuous variables with the
#   'simulated annealing' algorithm", ACM TOMS 13(3), 262-280 (1987),
#   doi:10.1145/29380.29864, plus its Corrigenda (ACM TOMS 15(3), 287
#   (1989)).  Local copies used for this transcription (2026-08-24):
#   SIMULATED_ANNEALING/Literature/29380.29864.pdf and 66888.356281.pdf.
# Transcription notes:
# * The rows below are the paper's Table II (p. 277): every SA run on the
#   parabolic multiminima function q_n, one row per starting point.  The
#   "Function evaluation x 10^-3" column is stored here as raw counts
# * Block headers transcribed from Table II: 2-D and 4-D runs used
#   T0 = 1E8, eps = 1E-4, s = .2, t = .05 with the Section-2 defaults
#   10-D block used T0 = 1E9, eps = 1E-4, s = .1, t = .04, NS = 15,
#   NT = 60.  Domains are (-10000, 10000)^n (p. 276); the steepness
#   vectors d and c_r = 0.15 (p. 272) are coded in
#   test_anneal_corana_protocol.cpp with the same page citation.
# * Three 4-D starting points are printed with doubled digits in the
#   scan (e.g. "-9999" / "10000").  They are resolved here using the
#   paper's own statement that starts lie "at a distance of about
#   1000*sqrt(n) from the origin" (p. 276): the resolved coordinates
#   give norms 1998.5, 2000 (exact), and 1999.2, while the literal
#   doubled-digit readings give norms > 10000 (and 10000 itself is the
#   domain boundary).  Resolved rows: (-999,-999,-999,-1000),
# * The paper's Table I (Rosenbrock, n = 2 and 4) is NOT transcribed:
#   its termination epsilon is not published, so those runs cannot be
#   replicated faithfully.  The rosenbrock builder in the test (classic
#   form, signs per the Corrigenda) stays available should the missing
#   epsilon ever surface.
# * The accuracy gate encodes the paper's reported outcomes: in 2-D
#   every run ended at 4.2E-10..4.0E-8 (gate 1E-6, far below the
#   nearest local minimum 3.375E-3); in 4-D eight of ten runs found the
#   global minimum (~E-7) and two stopped at the nearest local minimum
#   3.375E-3 (gate 4E-3; the test additionally requires at least half
#   of the 4-D runs to reach 1E-6); in 10-D every run stopped at the
#   nearest local minima valued 5.4E-4 (gate 6E-4 -- finding the global
#   minimum would also pass).
# Columns (tab-separated; one row per paper run):
#   function  rosenbrock | staircase
#   dim       problem dimension of the paper run
#   low,high  uniform search bounds of the paper run (scalars)
#   start     starting point: comma-separated list (dim values) or one
#             value replicated across dimensions
#   fs,ft     staircase grid step s_i and hole half-width t_i for the
#             run ("-" for rosenbrock)
#   v0        paper's initial step size (absolute, original units);
#             "-" = implementation default (Table II does not publish
#             v0; the step vector self-adapts every NS cycles)
#   t_init    paper's starting temperature T0 for the run
#   rt        temperature reduction coefficient r_T
#   ns        step-adjustment cycle length N_S
#   nt        temperature-step length N_T (adjustments per temperature)
#   neps      termination window N_eps
#   eps       termination tolerance epsilon
#   accuracy  gate on the final best f (see transcription notes)
#   neval     paper's reported number of function evaluations
# Acceptance policy applied by the test (fixed in code, not here):
#   every run ends with best f <= accuracy; per row, the mean eval
#   count lies within [0.5x, 2x] of neval; at least half of the
#   (staircase, 4-D) runs reach 1E-6 (paper: 8/10).
